- **Top jaw** (`desk + t` at the tip, running back to the spine at x = −t): a horizontal arm `t` thick that hooks over the top of the desk and reaches `jaw = 15 mm` onto it. Its last two points (`jaw − 2 mm, desk − grip` … `jaw, desk + 1 mm`) form the **grip bump and lead-in** — a 0.6 mm upturn that pinches the board's underside and a ramp so the clip can be pushed on.
- **Spine** (the vertical run at x = −t from `desk + t` down to `−2·t − cable`): the back wall joining the two jaws; it's what flexes when the clip is pushed on, so its thickness `t = 3 mm` sets the grip force.
- **Cable channel** (the stepped run under the spine: `cable + t` down to `−2·t − cable`, then the lip back up to `cable, −t − cable`): an 8 mm-wide open groove underneath, sized to the cable, with a raised lip (`cable + t` … `cable`, at height `−t − cable/2`) that keeps the cable captive but lets it slide in from the side.
- **Bottom jaw** (`jaw, −t` back to `jaw, −1 mm`): mirrors the top jaw under the board, ending in its own lead-in (`jaw, −1 mm` → `jaw − 2 mm, grip` → `jaw − 4 mm, 0`) so the desk's underside slides in past the bump.
- **Desk face** (the run along z = 0 to `z = desk` at x = 0): the flat that the jaws grip against — the clip's opening here is `desk + 2·grip ≈ 19.2 mm`, i.e. the 18 mm board is gripped 0.6 mm per side, inside the 0.4–0.8 mm rule.

Everything is written in the five params (`desk`, `cable`, `w`, `t`, `jaw`, `grip`), so changing the desk thickness moves both jaws symmetrically — DOF is 0, all corners parametric. The extrude is just `w = 12 mm` along the desk edge.

answer:
From the front you see exactly why this is a one-sketch part: the whole side profile is a single closed C, or rather a **hook — an open jaw facing right (toward the desk), with a cable channel folded underneath it**. Reading the 18 points of `outline` in script.js in order:

**The spine and top jaw (the C's back and upper arm).** From the outer tip of the top jaw at `['jaw', 'desk + t']` the outline runs left over the spine `['-t', 'desk + t']`, then down the back at x = −`t` to `['-t', '-2*t - cable']`. That vertical back wall, 3 mm thick (`t`), is the structural leaf of the clip: everything flexes against it. The top jaw reaches `jaw` = 15 mm onto the desk's top surface, and its last two points (`desk − grip`, then `desk + 1 mm`) are the **grip bump and its lead-in** — the small notch visible at the top-right of the drawing. The bump pinches the board by `grip` (0.6 mm) so the clip holds; the sloped face in front of it spreads the jaws as you push the clip on.

**The bottom jaw and its tip (the lower arm).** Coming back up the inside, the outline runs along the desk's underside at z = 0 out to `jaw`, then steps down 1 mm and ramps back to z = 0 through `['jaw − 2 mm', 'grip']` and `['jaw − 4 mm', 0]` — that's the mirrored bump/lead-in pair on the bottom jaw, visible as the small step low on the right. Both jaw tips use the same `grip` param, so tightening one jaw tightens both.

**The cable channel (the hook's curl).** From the desk's underside at `[0, 0]` the outline turns up the desk's edge face to `[0, 'desk']` (that's the face the notes call `body/side[side.outline.14]`, which sits against the desk edge), then folds under: out to `cable + t`, up the lip, and back into the pocket between z = −`t`−`cable` and −`t`−`cable/2`. That L-shaped pocket under the bottom jaw is the channel the cable snaps into; its width is `cable` (8 mm) and its roof is the underside of the jaw. In the drawing it's the small rectangular tongue poking into the cavity at bottom right.

So the outline does three jobs with one loop: **clamp** (two jaws with grip bumps and lead-ins pinching the 18 mm board), **attach** (the edge face and the jaw tops bear on the desk), and **hold** (the channel underneath keeps the lead from sliding off). And because every corner is written in the five params — `desk`, `cable`, `w`, `t`, `jaw`, `grip` — the whole family comes from that one loop: the notes' [fit-it-to-25 mm](lab:param?name=desk&value=25 mm) move slides the top jaw and nothing else.

The side elevation you get by looking along **X** is a plain $12 \times 35$ mm rectangle — that is just the two caps of the extrude. The shape lives in the profile, which is drawn on XZ, so it reads from the **front** elevation ([view](lab:view?name=front)): a **C-shaped push-on bracket with a hook hanging off its bottom jaw**, 18 mm deep (x = −3 … 15) by 35 mm tall (z = −14 … 21), 240.4 mm² of outline × 12 mm wide (exact B-rep, all params at script values). Eighteen segments close it, so it comes out as 18 side walls + 2 caps = 20 faces.

Walking it by what each zone does (areas are exact; the numbers are the sketch coordinates in mm, x into the desk, z up):

- **The mouth of the C — the two jaws** (outline.1, .15, .13, .9, .18, .10). The desk slot is the open pocket on the +x side, flats at z = 0 and z = 18 exactly `desk` apart, each jaw reaching `jaw` = 15 mm onto the board and 3 mm = `t` thick. 18 mm of flat bearing face underneath (outline.13, 132 mm²) and on top (outline.15, 132 mm²).
- **The pinch and the lead-ins** (outline.11, .12, .16, .17). At the jaw tips the mouth is chamfered out to 20 mm, then two 51° ramps (outline.11, .17) come in to a crest 2 mm from the tip at z = 0.6 and 17.4 — the `grip` bumps, 0.6 mm into the board each side, so the jaws spread as you push on and the slot only closes to `desk` 4 mm in. These are the two sloped faces 25–31 mm² each.
- **The spine** (outline.2, 420 mm²) — the back, x = −3, running the full 35 mm: one flat outside face, 3 mm wall, and its inner side (outline.14, 216 mm², x = 0, z = −3 … 18) is the registration face that sits flat against the desk's edge.
- **The cable hook** (outline.3 – .8). Below the bottom jaw the outline drops 11 mm to a floor at z = −14 (outline.3, underside), turns forward under the cable, and rises again as a lip 3 mm thick and 7 mm tall at x = 8 … 11. Between that lip, the back wall at x = 0 and the underside of the bottom jaw (outline.9) it leaves an 8 × 8 mm channel (`cable` wide) that opens forward: a cable threads in under the jaw from the front, drops behind the lip and can't slide out. The lip's inner face (outline.6) and the pocket floor (outline.7, 96 mm²) are what stop it.

Every one of those corners is an expression in [script.js](lab:open?file=script.js&line=7) — six points depend on `desk`, four on `grip`, five on `cable` — so the whole silhouette is a family: raise `desk` and the top jaw lifts, the spine and hook stay put. Nothing thinner than `t` = 3 mm anywhere, and every jaw has its ramped lead-in.

I'll read the script and look at the side profile.



The sheet's *side* axis looks along X, so it only shows the extrude's Y×Z rectangle. The profile lives in XZ — that's the **front** view. Let me draw that.



**The profile is the front view, not the side.** The outline is sketched on XZ ([script.js:6](lab:open?file=script.js&line=6)) and extruded 12 mm along Y, so the workbench's *side* view only shows that 12 × 35 rectangle; the shape below is what the [front view](lab:view?name=front) draws. Both come from `check()` at the script's own values (front's own overrides there are none), exact B-rep.

**The shape** is a squared **C opening to the right** — a spine against the desk edge, two jaws reaching onto the board, plus a small **hook** hanging under the spine at the bottom right. Overall 18 × 35 mm in this plane (x from −3 to +15, z from −14 to +21); the desk's edge sits at x = 0 and the board (z from 0 to 18) is the empty rectangle the C closes around.

Going round the outline ([script.js:7–28](lab:open?file=script.js&line=7)), with `desk 18`, `t 3`, `cable 8`, `jaw 15`, `grip 0.6`:

| segment | from → to | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| top outer | (15, 21) → (−3, 21) | outer face of the top jaw, a `t` = 3 mm wall above the board's top face |
| spine | (−3, 21) → (−3, −14) | the back wall, `t` thick off the desk edge, running the full 35 mm height |
| hook floor | (−3, −14) → (11, −14) | underside of the hook, 11 mm below the board |
| lip outer | (11, −14) → (11, −7) | the front of the cable lip, 3 mm wide, standing up to 7 mm below the board |
| lip top | (11, −7) → (8, −7) | lip crown — this is the **retention edge** that keeps a cable from falling out |
| lip inner | (8, −7) → (8, −11) | inner face of the lip; with the floor at −11 this makes the channel 8 × 8 mm, closing on the desk side at the spine |
| channel floor / spine inner | (8, −11) → (0, −11) → (0, −3) | floor and back of the cable channel, and the spine's inner face |
| bottom jaw underside | (0, −3) → (15, −3) | the ceiling of the channel mouth: the mouth is the 4 mm gap between z = −3 and the lip crown at −7 |
| bottom jaw tip | (15, −3) → (15, −1) → (13, 0.6) → (11, 0) | **lead-in**: the tip flares 1 mm clear of the board and ramps up onto a 0.6 mm grip bump at x ≈ 13 |
| board underside | (11, 0) → (0, 0) → (0, 18) | jaw inner face at z = 0 exactly, and the desk edge up to the top |
| top jaw inner | (0, 18) → (11, 18) → (13, 17.4) → (15, 19) | mirror of the bottom: flat at z = 18, a 0.6 mm bump biting at x ≈ 13, then a lead-in opening to 19 at the tip |

So three functions share one outline: the **two jaws** (3 mm walls, 15 mm reach) pinch the 18 mm board only at their 0.6 mm bumps, and both tips flare outward so the clip slides on rather than needing to be lined up; the **spine** is the 3 mm back wall that sets the grip depth; the **hook** below is a 4 mm-mouth cable channel, 8 × 8 mm, retained by the lip whose crown stops 7 mm under the board.

Because the whole thing is one closed polyline of expressions, changing `desk` alone slides the top jaw up and re-dates nothing below it, while `cable` deepens the hook and `t` thickens spine, jaws and lip together — the grip bumps scale only with `grip`, so the 0.4–0.8 mm rule stays put when the board changes.

The side profile of the open program (exact B‑rep, `run()` at the script's own values) is a **hooked “C” on a boot**: a vertical back spine, two horizontal jaws reaching onto the desk, and below the lower jaw a shallow cable channel closed by a standing lip. It fits in 18 × 12 × 35 mm (x from −3 to 15, z from −14 to 21); the sketch `side` lies on XZ with x running into the desk and z up, and `body` extrudes it 12 mm along −Y — so the drafting sheet's [front view](lab:view?name=front) is the outline as drawn (the `side` view just shows the 12 × 35 rectangle).

| x, z corners | face | what that piece of the outline does |
|---|---|---|
| (15,21)→(−3,21) `outline.1` | `body/side[side.outline.1]` | top of the top jaw, 18 mm of flat back-to-tip |
| (−3,21)→(−3,−14) `outline.2` | outer back face | the spine's outside, 35 mm tall, the full height of the clip |
| (−3,−14)→(11,−14) `outline.3` | bottom of the hook | underside of the cable cradle, 14 mm long |
| (11,−14)→(11,−7) `outline.4` | lip, outer face | the standing lip that stops the cable dropping out |
| (11,−7)→(8,−7)→(8,−11)→(0,−11) `outline.5–7` | channel floor/back | the notch of the cable channel: 3 mm wide × 4 mm tall, 8 mm deep, open to +X |
| (0,−11)→(0,−3) `outline.8` | inside face of the hook | wall between the channel and the desk edge |
| (0,−3)→(15,−3) `outline.9` | underside of bottom jaw | the bottom jaw's outer skin, 15 mm |
| (15,−3)→(15,−1)→(13,0.6) `outline.10–11` | tip face + lead-in | 2 mm blunt tip, then the ramp the board's bottom edge rides to spread the jaw |
| (13,0.6)→(11,0) `outline.12` | grip bump | the 0.6 mm bump that bites into the board |
| (11,0)→(0,0) `outline.13` | slot floor | flat face resting on the board's underside behind the bump |
| (0,0)→(0,18) `outline.14` | slot back | the face pressed flat against the [desk edge](lab:face?name=body/side[side.outline.14]), exactly `desk` tall |
| (0,18)→(11,18)→(13,17.4)→(15,19) `outline.15–17` | slot roof + bump + lead-in | the top jaw's mirror of the same three moves |
| (15,19)→(15,21) `outline.18` | tip face | 2 mm top jaw tip |

So the parts of the outline are: the **spine** (x −3…0) that wraps the edge; the **desk slot** (x 0…15, z 0…`desk`), open to the right, whose back wall is `outline.14`; the **two jaws** (3 mm = `t` each) whose tips carry the grip bump and, in front of it, a sloped lead-in, so the jaws can be sprung on; and the **hook** below (z −14…−3) with the **cable channel** — a sideways-opening slot `cable/2` tall by `cable` deep, roofed by the bottom jaw and lipped at x = `cable + t`.

Every one of those 18 corners is an expression of the six params in [script.js:28](lab:open?file=script.js&line=28), which is why the whole outline moves as a family: change `desk` and only the slot's roof, the slot back and the top jaw shift, e.g. [desk = 25 mm](lab:param?name=desk&value=25%20mm).
